plain_description.what: An LLM wrote a grading guide (a rubric) for multiple-choice questions from the same 40 training examples, using a corrected prompt and an automatic screen for unwanted wording. The aim was a rubric for the new judge design.
plain_description.why: The judge needs a rubric that does not bias its verdicts, and the first attempt had been rejected.
plain_description.information: A fit rubric could go into the new judge. An unfit one shows that the induction step or the screen is still flawed. Result: done. The rubric passed every automatic check on the first try, but a reviewer judged it unfit: it defines correctness as matching a reference answer that is itself wrong on 133 of 1,027 items, and it rewards visible reasoning. It was not adopted, and this registration will not be re-tried. The author then registered a separate new induction with a revised prompt. It makes no claim about rubric value or accuracy, and it shows that the automatic screen is weak evidence of fitness.
